newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle tumble late, close weak.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle tumble late, close weak.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures tumbled late to close weak as long liquidation pushed live cattle futures down into fund sell stops, traders said.

Although bitter cold temperatures continued to provide support to December live cattle, that month also slipped on spreading of long February/short December. Much of the break was attributed to lack of followthrough support on the early advance and technical resistance, traders said.
Weakness also followed increased fed cattle sales at $65 per cwt and projections on Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report, they said.
The upturn in boxed beef also lent some early support before running into the technical resistance, they said.

Early estimates on the cattle report for major feedlots of 1,000 head or more point to on-feed numbers on December 1 between 102 to 104.2 percent of a year ago, November placements between 98 and 109 percent and marketings between 91 and 98 percent of last year.
RBH and Refco spread long February/short December late. R.J. O'Brien and Cargill Investor Services sold February, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, there was mixed hedging and commission house selling of April 66 to 70 calls early. Commission houses sold February 64 calls on the break in futures. Volatility was steady in February and steady to weak in April. In feeder options, Fimat Futures USA sold January 66 calls, pit sources added.

Feeders continued following live cattle and weakened late with higher corn futures also weighing on sentiment and offsetting early support from a higher CME feeder cattle index. Sell stops and reversing feeding margin spreads, long live cattle/short feeders, added to losses, traders said.

Locals sold with some light pressure also evident from Fimat selling March and April. LFG sell stops were touched off in January. ING was a buyer. Cargill spread long June live cattle/short March feeders and Stone Traders bought June cattle and sold January feeders, pit sources said.
The latest index was up $0.56 at $65.58 per cwt.
Live cattle closed 0.725 cent lower to 0.175 higher with February off most at 63.250 cents. Feeder cattle were off 0.675 to 0.100 with January off most at 65.825 cents.
